body:
MEASURED, on the operator's own Clara BW (4.45.23792) and deployed server,
2026-08-18. This supersedes an earlier SPECULATIVE reading of the same code —
the mapping is now established, not inferred.

`cps/services/kobo_import.py`:

    _COLOR_MAP = {0: "yellow", 1: "red", 2: "green", 3: "blue"}
    ...
    color=_COLOR_MAP.get(color or 0, "yellow")

The real device mapping, measured by serving each palette hex in an authored
response and reading `Bookmark.Color` back:

    wire highlightColor   Bookmark.Color
    #F6F3B3               0    yellow
    #E8AFCF               1    pink
    #B2E1E8               2    blue
    #C6E09E               3    green
    #A0A0A0               4    grey   <- what a Clara BW produces organically

So the table is wrong three ways:

1. NO ENTRY FOR 4. A greyscale Clara BW writes Color=4 for every organic
   highlight. Measured on the device right now: all 17 highlight rows are
   Color=4 (the 13 dogears are Color=0). Every one of them imports as
   "yellow" via the `.get(..., "yellow")` default.
2. 2 AND 3 ARE SWAPPED — 2 is blue, not green; 3 is green, not blue.
3. 1 IS MISLABELLED — it is pink; Kobo has no red.

Defaulting an unrecognised int to yellow is the aggravating factor: it invents
a specific wrong colour rather than recording "unknown", so nothing downstream
can tell a real yellow from a failed lookup.

THE TEST PINS THE BUG. `tests/unit/test_annotations_import_endpoint.py::
test_color_round_trips` asserts `bm-002 == "red"` and `bm-003 == "green"` —
i.e. it restates `_COLOR_MAP` back to itself. Nothing round-trips; the name is
aspirational. A correct fix makes that test fail, and that is the tell it was
pinning the implementation rather than the behaviour.

WHY THIS IS NOT A ONE-LINE FIX, and what has to be decided first: the
`annotation.highlight_color` column currently holds THREE vocabularies at once,
measured on the deployed server:

    #F6F3B3  kobo       562     <- live PATCH path stores the WIRE HEX
    #E8AFCF  kobo        20
    #B2E1E8  kobo        17
    #C6E09E  kobo         5
    #A0A0A0  kobo         8
    (null)   kobo         9
    red      webreader    4     <- web reader stores a NAME

and the import stores names from the table above. Meanwhile
`WEBREADER_COLORS = ("yellow", "red", "green", "blue")` contains `red`, which
the Kobo palette does not have, and lacks `pink` and `grey`, which it does.
`_data_json_row` passes whatever it finds straight to the UI as
`r.highlight_color or "yellow"`.

So correcting `_COLOR_MAP` in isolation would emit `pink`/`grey`, which the
web reader's palette cannot render, and swapping green/blue changes colours
users already see. The decision needed is which vocabulary the column speaks —
wire hex (what 612 of 616 kobo rows already hold) is the obvious candidate,
with the web reader normalising on read.

Recorded rather than patched because the correct fix is a representation
decision, not a lookup-table edit, and a half fix here changes user-visible
colour for the worse.

resolution.note: Fixed by #1737 (squashed as a751f648c). cps/services/annotation_colors.py is now the one hex<->name table, measured on the operator's Clara BW: Bookmark.Color 0-4 -> #F6F3B3 yellow / #E8AFCF pink / #B2E1E8 blue / #C6E09E green / #A0A0A0 grey. The column stores the canonical wire hex and every read path normalises to a display name; an unrecognised code resolves to NULL rather than an invented yellow, and no migration ships because the normaliser tolerates all three legacy vocabularies on read. RED/GREEN: the author's suite went 86 failed -> 213 passed with the fix stashed and restored, and the same A/B was re-observed on a live container - main answered /annotations/11/data.json with the raw hex and 'yellow' for a NULL column, this branch answers yellow/pink/blue/green/grey and null, on identical rows and the identical request. VERIFIED IN A BROWSER, by computed style, on all six render surfaces (SPA highlights page, SPA reader marks and drawer, classic annotations_view.html, legacy epub/PDF/comic renderers): each wire hex renders as its intended colour, a NULL renders as the #d0cbc2 neutral (var(--border) on the highlights page) and is never repainted yellow, and the 4 legacy webreader 'red' rows still read back red. Driven through the real /annotations/import upload for Color 0,1,2,3,4,7,NULL - stored as the five hexes plus two NULLs, displayed as the five names plus two nulls. Note-save on an imported grey highlight now PATCHes 200 with no colour in the body, where the payload main's client built for the same row (highlight_color 'a0a0a0') still 400s bad_color. Deferred, unchanged: F-0eb843 (the KOReader cwasync Lua provider still holds the wrong table). New: F-8efa11 (safeColorToken can strip an unknown token into a palette name).

title: The KoboReader.sqlite import assigns the wrong highlight colour, and every Clara BW highlight imports as yellow
